paragraphs: The fifty cent coin is the largest of the gold coloured euro pieces, and its edge is what identifies it in a hand: a coarse scalloped milling quite unlike the fine reeding on other denominations. The French obverse carries a sower figure rather than a monarch, which places it precisely.
The mesh is efficient at 11,920 polygons and 11,922 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, with the relief and the edge scalloping built as geometry so light catches them properly.

At $19 it suits financial and banking visualisation, currency and payment material, advertising and product renders, scale references and games. Real-world scale is kept, so it sits correctly in a pile of change. On sale since 2024.

A branded delivery box is one of the most recognisable objects in domestic life, and it is deliberately plain: brown corrugated card, printed in one colour, with a tape strip down the seam. That plainness is what makes the branding read from across a hallway.

The mesh is minimal at 1,712 polygons and 1,800 vertices, built entirely from quads with non-overlapping UVs, and ships with 2 texture maps at 4096x4096 carrying the corrugation, the print and the tape.
At $19 it suits e-commerce and delivery visualisation, logistics and courier marketing, hallway and doorstep scenes, retail advertising and games. On sale since 2019.

A feeding bottle is designed around the teat: a wide neck so the teat can be seated and a collar that screws over it, with graduated markings up the side and a shape narrow enough for small hands. Every one of those features is regulated or ergonomic rather than decorative.
The mesh is light at 6,906 polygons and 3,507 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, with the teat and the collar as separate bodies so the bottle can be shown assembled or apart.

At $19 and built to CheckMate specification, it suits baby care product visualisation, packaging and brand mockups, nursery and family interiors, pharmacy and e-commerce renders, and games. On sale since 2024.

An unopened tub of ice cream has a smooth swirled surface that has never been scooped, and that untouched state is a specific and useful thing: it is what a product photograph shows, while a scooped tub belongs in a kitchen scene. The two are quite different assets.
The mesh is light at 14,016 polygons and 13,984 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, with the geometry in the surface swirl and the tub rim.
At $19 it suits frozen food and dessert advertising, packaging and brand mockups, supermarket freezer and e-commerce renders, food photography set dressing, and games. On sale since 2022.

A vehicle silhouette is an icon in three dimensions: a solid black profile with no surface detail, used where a real car would be too specific or too distracting. Infographics, wayfinding, parking signage and interface work all need vehicles reduced to a shape rather than rendered.
The mesh is minimal at 5,340 polygons and 5,295 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, which is exactly the budget an icon should carry.

A van and a mini truck silhouette sit on this page at the same $19. All suit infographic and data visualisation, wayfinding and signage design, motion graphics, interface and app work, and games. Built to CheckMate specification, on sale since 2024.

A rubber floor mat is shaped to a specific footwell, with raised edges to hold water, a moulded tread pattern and anchor points that engage clips in the carpet. Those anchors matter: an unsecured mat can slide under a pedal, which is why they are moulded in rather than optional.
The mesh runs 22,730 polygons and 24,460 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, with almost all of the geometry in the tread pattern.
At $19 it suits automotive accessory marketing, vehicle interior visualisation, parts retail and catalogue renders, workshop scenes and games. On sale since 2017.

A blade fuse is colour coded by rating, which is the only way to tell one from another at a glance, and the transparent body exists so the element inside can be checked without a meter. Those two facts are the entire design, and both have to be visible in a model for it to be useful.
The mesh is light at 11,970 polygons and 11,970 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, and ships with 6 texture maps at 4096x4096 carrying the tinted plastic and the printed rating.
At $19 it suits automotive parts marketing and catalogues, workshop and diagnostic visualisation, technical illustration, retail renders and games. On sale since 2020.

A dent puller works by pressing a rubber cup against a panel and levering the air out of it, so the tool is essentially a suction cup with a cam handle. Shown open, the cup is relaxed and the handle is up, which is the state it is in when it is placed rather than pulling.
The mesh is light at 8,352 polygons and 4,182 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, with the geometry in the cup, the cam and the handle.
At $19 and built to CheckMate specification, it suits automotive repair visualisation, bodyshop and workshop scenes, tool retail and catalogue renders, DIY material and games. On sale since 2023.

This handset uses a leather effect back rather than glass, which is unusual and immediately visible: the surface has a grain and a matte finish, and there is a stitched seam line across it. That texture is the differentiator in a market where almost every phone is a glass slab.
The mesh is efficient at 34,886 polygons and 18,469 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, with the geometry in the camera island, the button cutouts and the frame chamfers.
At $19 it suits consumer electronics visualisation, product and e-commerce renders, mobile marketing material, desk and lifestyle scenes, and games. On sale since 2023.

An institutional ceiling fitting is a bare fluorescent or LED batten in a reflector housing, hung on chains or fixed flush, with no diffuser to speak of. That utilitarian quality is what dates and places an interior instantly as a school, a corridor or a workshop rather than a home.
The mesh is light at 11,596 polygons and 5,952 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, with the geometry in the reflector, the tube housing and the fixings.
At $19 it suits school and institutional interior visualisation, architectural and educational renders, film and television set dressing, lighting catalogue material and games. On sale since 2023.

A lateral flow kit is a small set of very specific pieces: a sealed cassette with a sample well and a result window, a dropper of buffer, a swab in a wrapper and a printed instruction leaflet. It became one of the most widely recognised medical objects in the world within a matter of months.

The mesh is minimal at 2,689 polygons and 2,778 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, and ships with 5 texture maps at 4096x4096 carrying the printed cassette, the packaging and the leaflet.

At $19 and built to StemCell specification, it suits public health and medical visualisation, diagnostics marketing, news and documentary graphics, pharmacy and clinic scenes, and games. On sale since 2020.

A shikara is a long flat wooden boat with a canopy over the middle, cushions inside and a heart shaped paddle. It is built for calm lake water rather than for open river, which is why the hull is shallow and the freeboard is so low - and why it is inseparable from the lake it works on.
The mesh runs 57,465 polygons and 57,477 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, with the geometry in the canopy frame, the seating and the carved decoration.

At $19 and built to StemCell specification, it suits travel and tourism material, cultural and heritage visualisation, lake and waterfront scenes, documentary and editorial imagery, and games. On sale since 2025.

A disposable lighter is a transparent tank with a metal hood over the top, a serrated flint wheel and a lever. Everything about it is designed to cost almost nothing to make, which is why the tank is uncoloured plastic and why the fuel level is visible - it is cheaper to show it than to hide it.

The mesh runs 36,500 polygons and 36,509 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, and ships with 12 texture maps at 4096x4096 carrying the translucent tank, the metal hood and the printing.
At $19 it suits everyday object visualisation, retail and convenience store renders, character set dressing for film, television and games, still life and editorial imagery. On sale since 2017.

A roll of foam tape is a cylinder with a liner on one face, and the interesting part is the end of the roll: the liner tab peeled slightly back so the tape reads as usable rather than as a solid disc. Without that detail it is just a ring.

The mesh is minimal at 832 polygons and 832 vertices, built entirely from quads with non-overlapping UVs, which is exactly the right economy for a subject whose realism comes from the material rather than from geometry.
At $19 it suits industrial and DIY product visualisation, tool and hardware retail renders, workshop and workbench scenes, packaging mockups and games. On sale since 2022.
